title: La porta della subordinata
summary: Joining sentences with perché, quando, and se — the gate from A2 into real B1 sentences

blocks.title: Perché — not just 'why?'
blocks.body: You already know *perché* as a question word ('why?'). It doubles as **'because'** in the answer — just place the reason clause right after: *Non vengo perché sono stanco.* (I'm not coming because I'm tired.) One little word joins two full sentences into one.
blocks.callout: *Perché* asks 'why?' and answers 'because' — same word, both jobs.

items.en: I'm staying home because it's raining.
I'm not going out because I'm tired.

blocks.title: Quando — when two futures meet
blocks.body: *Quando* means 'when.' Italian-specific trick: when **both** actions are in the future, Italian puts **both verbs in the futuro** — English doesn't. English says 'When it rains, I'll stay home' (present + future); Italian says *Quando pioverà, resterò a casa* (futuro + futuro).
blocks.callout: Both future → both futuro. Don't borrow English's present-tense shortcut here.

pairs.left: English: *When it rains, I'll stay home.* (present + future)
pairs.right: Italiano: *Quando pioverà, resterò a casa.* (futuro + futuro)
pairs.note: Italian keeps both halves in the futuro when both events lie ahead.

blocks.prompt: Complete: 'Quando ___ a Roma, ti scriverò.' (When I arrive in Rome, I'll write you.)
blocks.explain: Both halves point to the future, so Italian uses the futuro in both: *arriverò… ti scriverò.*

blocks.title: Se — real conditions
blocks.body: *se* means 'if.' For real, likely conditions, just line up ordinary tenses: present + present for a general habit (*Se piove, resto a casa* — if it rains, I stay home), or futuro + futuro for one specific future case (*Se farà caldo, andremo al mare*). Save the trickier 'what if I were…' hypotheticals for Week 9's periodo ipotetico.
blocks.callout: Real 'if', ordinary tenses — the tricky hypothetical *se* waits until Week 9.

lines.en: If it rains, I stay home.

lines.nl: Se farà caldo, andremo al mare.
lines.en: If it's hot, we'll go to the sea.
If you have time, call me.

blocks.prompt: Join into one sentence with perché: 'I don't go out. It's raining.'
blocks.hint: perché + the reason, right after the main clause.
blocks.explain: *Non esco perché piove.* — main clause, then perché + reason.

blocks.prompt: Listen and type the whole line.

blocks.scene: Sofia tells you her weekend plan, weather permitting.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.nl: Se farà bel tempo sabato, andrò al mare con la moto.
lines.en: If the weather's nice Saturday, I'll go to the seaside on my scooter.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.nl: Se pioverà, resterò a casa e guarderò un film.
lines.en: If it rains, I'll stay home and watch a movie.
lines.spotlight: se + futuro, futuro — a real future condition, both halves matching.

lines.speaker: You
lines.en: When will you know the forecast?

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.nl: Le guarderò stasera, quando tornerò a casa.
lines.en: I'll check tonight, when I get home.
lines.spotlight: quando + futuro again — tornerò, not torno, because it's still ahead of us.

blocks.prompt: Write three sentences about your week using perché (why/because), quando (when — remember, futuro + futuro!), and se (if).
